name: Corruption
overview: Scripture reveals corruption primarily as the physical decay that follows death, as seen in Genesis 3:19 and Job 34:15, where man returns to dust and flesh perishes. This physical decomposition is accompanied by imagery of worms and decay in Job 17:14 and 21:26, underscoring the reality of mortality. Beyond the physical, corruption also carries a figurative sense related to sin and moral blemish, as Leviticus 22:25 warns against offering anything with corruption, symbolizing impurity unacceptable to God. Additionally, Psalms 16:10 highlights God's power over corruption by affirming that He will not allow His Holy One to see decay, pointing to the hope of resurrection and divine preservation.
